title: AI system register entry
description: One entry in the inventory of AI systems and models: who owns it, what it may do, how it is classified and where its evidence lives. The deploy pipeline writes the core fields; intake adds the classification. Extends the registry entry shape in chapter 05 (id, version, owner, scope, expiry).
$comment: AI Governance Engineer templates and schemas library, v1. CC BY 4.0 (attribution: Jorge García Aibar). x-evidences names the obligations a field or record helps evidence: an illustrative mapping, not a claim of conformity and not legal advice. https://aigovernanceengineer.com/resources/templates

$schema.description: The URI of this schema, so a record says what it claims to be.

id.description: Stable registry identifier, lower case (for example "credit-afford-03"). Never reused after retirement.

version.description: Version of the deployed artefact this entry describes (a date, a semantic version or a build id).

owner.description: Accountable owning team or role. An entry without an owner is denied production access.

scope.description: Declared scope: the permissions, data domains or decisions the system is allowed to touch. Anything outside it is out of policy.

expiry.description: Date after which the entry must be renewed or the system is deactivated. Forces a periodic review.

purpose.description: Intended purpose in one or two sentences, as the use-case record states it.

system_type.description: What kind of AI artefact this is.

role.description: The organisation's role for this system under the EU AI Act. Recheck it whenever the system is modified or rebranded.

risk_classification.description: Regulatory and internal classification, with the record that justifies it.

eu_ai_act_category.description: Classification under the EU AI Act, from the classification decision record.

annex_iii_point.description: For Annex III systems, the point and letter relied on (for example "5(b)").

internal_tier.description: The organisation's own risk tier, which drives the controls required.

rationale.description: Why this classification, in one paragraph.

classification_record.description: Link to the signed classification decision.

lifecycle_stage.description: Where the system is in its lifecycle.

use_case_record.description: Id of the use-case record that admitted the system at intake.

components.description: Models, datasets, tools and services the system is built from. Mirrors the AIBOM.

ref.description: Identifier of the component (registry id, dataset id or package name).

aibom.description: Link to the AIBOM (for example a CycloneDX ML-BOM).

jurisdictions.description: Countries or regions where the system is used (ISO 3166 codes where possible).

personal_data.description: Whether the system processes personal data. True routes it to the DPIA screen.

affected_persons.description: Categories of people affected by the outputs (for example "loan applicants").

human_oversight.description: Oversight mode designed into the system.

eu_database_registration.description: Registration in the EU database for high-risk systems.

required.description: Whether registration in the EU database applies.

registration_id.description: Identifier returned by the EU database, once registered.

evidence.description: Links to the records that evidence this entry: model card, impact assessments, eval results, go/no-go.

last_reviewed.description: When the entry was last reviewed by its owner.

public_record.description: Optional. What a public register or transparency record asks for that the internal entry does not: the responsible organisation, a contact, a plain-language description and the registration details. One source record then feeds a UK ATRS record, a Canada AIA, an EU database registration (Annex VIII) and a model or system card; the field crosswalk is on /toolkit/ai-register-entry.

organisation.description: Organisation responsible for the system (the provider or the deployer), as a public record names it.

address.description: The organisation's address and other contact details, where a register asks for them.

contact_email.description: Contact address of the team or organisation responsible: a role mailbox, not a person.

website_url.description: Public page with more information about the system.

one_sentence_description.description: The system in one plain-language sentence.

description.description: Plain-language overview for the public: what the system is and why it is used.

data_and_logic.description: Basic, concise description of the information the system uses (data, inputs) and of its operating logic.

trade_name.description: Trade name and any additional unambiguous reference that identifies and traces the system.

market_status.description: Status of the system on the market or in service.

region.description: Primary region or area whose public the system affects.

authorised_representative.description: Name and contact details of the authorised representative, where one is required.

certificate.description: Type, number and expiry date of any notified-body certificate, with the notified body's name or number.

declaration_of_conformity.description: Link to the EU declaration of conformity, where one exists.

instructions_for_use.description: Link to the electronic instructions for use.

extensions.description: Organisation-specific fields. Validators ignore their content; keep evidence-bearing fields in the core record.
